thread:
alexa: running the AWQ weight-only rollout on staging and seeing a weird tail: group_size=16 is fine but group_size=8 is ~7% slower than float baseline for short seqs (<=32). p99 spikes too. Anyone seen packing overhead blow up like this?

carlos: curious — is this on the nvlink cluster or the gpu-cloud nodes? packing can interact badly with kvcache prefetching.

alexa: cloud nodes (A100s). repro command: `python perf_microbench.py --model gpt2-small --quant awq --group 8 --seq 16 --batch 1 --cache on`

perf-bot: snapshot 2163456801: staging/awq-rollout: p50 +2%, p95 +9%, p99 +14% after deploy. CPU side shows increased memcpy time around pack/unpack.

ming: can you paste `nvprof`/traces? my hunch is unpack scatter loops suffer when group != multiple of lane size, so branch mispred + prefetcher thrash.

alexa: pasted a trimmed trace: 
```
Memcpy HtoD 0.12ms
pack_int8_kernel (grid 256x1) 0.74ms
unpack_kernel (grid 512x1) 1.35ms  <-- dominates for group=8
KV cache lookup 0.03ms
```

sam: interesting that unpack > pack. AWQ's layout for group=8 produces more strided writes on the unpack path. Could be cacheline blowouts. Have we tried round-robin lane placement (patch from last month)?

alexa: patched lane placement locally — latency down by ~3% but p99 still high. Also observed more frequent kvcache evictions during the AWQ runs; maybe packing increases working set and pushes kvcache thrash.

ira: tagging eng-runtime because kernel choice might need a fallback. @eng-runtime please advise on kernel selector heuristics for small seq / small batch combos.

carlos: for now add a lightweight heuristic: if group_size < 16 and seq <= 32 and batch ==1, prefer the serial-unpack kernel with vectorized inner loop (we have that as fallback). It costs a bit of steady throughput but avoids bad tail for p99.

ming: also add a quick profiler metric: `pack_stride_miss_ratio` and expose in console. That'll help correlate pack layout vs kvcache miss rate.

sam: agree. I'll add an A/B test in the rollout config: route 5% of traffic with the fallback kernel and collect p50/p95/p99 + kvcache hit rate + memcpy time.

alexa: started a microbench sweep: group 4/8/12/16, seq 8/16/32/64, batch 1/2. Early result: group=12 sometimes beats 16 for latency (weird), suggests grouping interacts with alignment/prefetch in non-monotonic way. I'll upload logs.

perf-bot: test upload complete: https://staging-perf/redwood/awq-sweep/2163456789

ira: thanks. once logs are in, eng-runtime can play with kernel-cost model to nudge selector. also file a short issue to track calibration->performance: AWQ calibrate step modifies byte layout; that should be part of performance regression tests.

alexa: filed issue RNW-Perf-1423 with sample reproducer and traces. moving to canary with fallback kernel now. :thumbsup:

sam: next steps: 1) add pack_stride_miss_ratio metric 2) rollout fallback 5% 3) autotune selector using microbench sweep data 4) add regression test blocking AWQ calibrations that change unpack stride patterns.

carlos: quick note — reprofile on slower seqs too. some kernels get faster as seq grows due to amortized unpack cost.

alexa: will do. thanks everyone.
